claims.claim: In Python, names refer to objects, and assignment is a name-binding operation.
Assignment statements can rebind a name; a previously bound name is rebound when assigned again.
Every Python object has an identity, type, and value; `is` compares identity.
Two names can refer to the same object, so rebinding one name does not by itself rebind the other.
Whether an object's value can change is a property of the object and its type, not a consequence of the variable-like name alone.
Python has no declarations in the execution-model sense; this lesson therefore teaches assignment as binding rather than a separate declaration step.
